method: Real documents, not PubChem grids: the pixel-exact method of build_ground_truth.py does not apply. Twenty-five recent pharmaceutical patents in the cardiovascular, metabolic/diabetes and renal therapeutic areas, priority dates 2012-2024. Every structure was located by reading the PDF itself - pdftoppm page renders at 45-400 dpi plus tesseract OCR of those renders, because 24 of the 25 documents have NO text layer at all. Each resolved molecule required TWO independent views to agree: a PubChem PUG-REST lookup keyed on something PRINTED IN THE DOCUMENT (an INN, a full systematic name, a compound code expanded elsewhere in the text) AND a reading of the drawing; where the document prints no name, the SMILES read off the drawing was submitted to PUG-REST /compound/smiles/ and accepted only when the returned InChIKey matched the hand reading exactly. Every SMILES round-trips through RDKit Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and its InChIKey was recomputed with RDKit and checked against PubChem's at manifest build time - that check caught three stereochemical transcription errors that inspection had passed. Per-molecule `confidence` is one of: name_match (a name printed in the document resolves to the CID and the drawing agrees), drawing_read (the document prints no name; the structure was read off the drawing and confirmed against a PubChem record by structure search), generic, or unresolved. `pixel_verified` is false everywhere - it is not achievable on real documents.
excluded: Structures that are DRAWN but carry no resolvable SMILES are held in each group's `unscoreable` array, NOT in `molecules`. That split is load-bearing: score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry of `molecules` and a null raises TypeError before its own error message. `unscoreable` holds Markush/R-group generics (generic: true) and structures with no second independent view (confidence: unresolved), including four cases where the printed NAME and the DRAWING disagree and neither can be used to check the other. Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row.
count_caveat: structures_drawn counts DEPICTIONS on the kept pages and is EXACT for every group in this round - there are no estimated counts here, because every document was trimmed down to pages whose depictions were counted box by box. The four count fields therefore do not sum: a compound drawn n times contributes n to structures_drawn and 1 to structures_resolved.

The wavy bond is the interesting one - it is a positive assertion that the centre is NOT defined, so the correct reference is the stereo-unspecified PubChem record, and a tool that reads the squiggle as a plain bond gets the same answer while a tool that reads it as a wedge gets a different, real, wrong record. Both intermediates resolve to stereo-unspecified CIDs.
